drafter: claude-opus-5-5 via Claude Code subagent (general-purpose), no tools used

lines.pattern: In week one, distorted guitars in a wall of sound took 43 of 68 plays and fingerpicked nylon guitar took 12. By week four, the wall of sound was down to 7 of 58 plays and the nylon guitar was up to 35.
lines.receipt: Distorted guitars: 43 of 68 week-one plays (63%) to 7 of 58 week-four plays (12%). Fingerpicked nylon guitar: 12 of 68 (18%) to 35 of 58 (60%).
offers: Did the quieter guitar arrive with a calmer stretch, something settling in that no longer needed the noise?
Or did the wall of sound start to feel like too much, so the softer guitar was a way to keep things low while you were worn out?

lines.pattern: Of 251 plays, 45 were of new tracks and 206 were of tracks that were not new. One new track, Lumen Tarry, was played 4 times in week four.
lines.receipt: 45 of 251 plays (18%) on new tracks; 206 of 251 (82%) on tracks that were not new; Lumen Tarry 4 plays in week four.
offers: Were the familiar tracks doing exactly what you wanted, so there was little reason to look further?
Or has there been little room lately for anything unfamiliar, and is Lumen Tarry, 4 plays in week four, the first time that room opened up?

lines.pattern: Of 251 plays across 25 distinct tracks, 108 went to three of them: Fennow Letter 47 times, Tamsel Lullaby 31 times and Cindergrist 30 times.
lines.receipt: 108 of 251 plays (43%) on 3 of 25 tracks: Fennow Letter 47, Tamsel Lullaby 31, Cindergrist 30.
offers: Do these three still give you something every time, so going back is a way of getting more of it?
Or were they something steady to hold on to through a month that felt restless?
